newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT shares seen consolidating after recent surge.
newsitem.headline: NTT shares seen consolidating after recent surge.

text.p: Shares in Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) are likely to consolidate for the time being after their winning streak in recent weeks, analysts said on Monday.

The telecommunications giant was in strong demand after Morgan Stanley announced at the end of April that it would include the issue in its capital international indices from the end of trade on Friday.
But after surging on Friday to hit 1.11 million yen, a new high for this calendar year, the share became subject to sales on Monday.
On Monday, NTT the price of shares closed 50,000 yen lower at 1.06 million yen.
"After the shares hit a high of 1.11 million yen on Friday, the price is likely to go sideways for a while," said Yasuo Ueki, a general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.

"After buying which was prompted by short-term demand, we are worried about a counter-reaction, and expectations of further (government) NTT share sales are making the bottom side vulnerable," said a trader at a foreign securities house.
Media reports earlier this year said the Finance Ministry planned to sell 500,000 government-owned NTT shares.
Following NTT's privatisation in 1985, the ministry sold 5.4 million NTT shares by March 1989, but has put off further sales since then due to a sluggish Tokyo stock market.
On Friday, UBS Securities Ltd analyst Toshiho Sato lowered her investment assessment of NTT to "neutral" from "buy".

But she also expects the shares to hover at a high level for a while until details of the ministry's plan to sell NTT shares are unveiled, adding that its earnings for the current business year to March 1998 would be solid.
On May 23, NTT reported healthy annual profit gains, as the world's largest phone company continued to benefit from increased cellular phone and Internet use.
It said parent current profit rose 11 percent to 366 billion yen in 1996/97, up from profits of 328.92 billion yen in 1995/96. -- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
